transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Um, thank you for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. I'm just here because... well, I've been having these little flashes, I guess you'd call them? It's probably nothing major, but they keep hitting me out of nowhere. Like, I'll just be standing at a pickup counter for work, and suddenly it's like I'm back in this... this crowded holding room. I keep seeing this fight that broke out, and hearing everyone getting shoved against the wall. It's silly that it's bothering me so much, but it's just a bit distracting, you know? Is that... does that make sense?
Did something specific happen to you in that crowded holding room?

Um... yeah. I... I really hope you don't think badly of me, it was honestly just a huge misunderstanding. But about a week ago, I was... well, I was detained overnight. I'm a courier, and I just got caught up in a situation while I was on a route, I swear I'm not a troublemaker or anything. 

But while I was stuck in that holding area, I ended up seeing this... this really awful assault happen right in front of me. And, um, ever since then—so for about a week now—I've just been having those little flashes I mentioned. I know I should probably just brush it off and be over it by now, right? I hope it's okay that I'm even bringing it up... did that answer your question, Doctor?
Have you been avoiding anything or any place because of what happened in the holding room?

Um... well, maybe just a little bit? I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I'm not doing my job or anything. I'm still working hard! But, um, I guess I have been turning down the night runs lately. And... well, I might be taking the long way around town sometimes, just to, you know, make sure I don't go anywhere near that detention building. 

I just... I can't really bring myself to go near it right now, or even talk about the details of what happened, because whenever I do, I just get that feeling like I'm right back in that room. I know it's probably silly, and I should just push through it, right? I'm sorry, I hope that doesn't make me sound weak or anything. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have you been having trouble sleeping since the incident in the holding room?

Um... yeah, sleep has been a little tricky. I really don't want to complain, because I know everyone gets tired, right? But... I guess I've barely been sleeping since it happened. I'll maybe doze off for an hour or two, but then I just wake up. Sometimes it's from a dream about being stuck in that cell, or even just hearing a door slam in my sleep, and my heart starts racing. 

And then by morning, I just feel completely wrecked. It's embarrassing to admit, because I really pride myself on being reliable, but I've been feeling almost too exhausted to safely drive my route. I'm sure I just need to try harder to relax at night, right? I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just making excuses... does that answer your question, Doctor?
Do you feel guilty about what happened in the holding room?

Um... guilty? I mean... no, not really. I hope that's the right answer. I know it wasn't my fault, because I was just... I was just sitting there, you know? I couldn't have stopped it. 

I guess... well, I mean, maybe a little part of me wishes I could have done something, but I don't think I feel guilty. I just... I just want to move past it and get back to being a good employee. I shouldn't feel guilty if I didn't do anything wrong, right? I hope that makes sense, Doctor. I really don't want to sound like a bad person.
Have you been feeling constantly on edge or irritable since the incident in the holding room?

Um... on edge? Well, I mean, I try really hard to be a team player, you know? I'm usually pretty easygoing. But, um... I guess maybe I have been a little bit more tense lately? I don't want you to think I'm a difficult person or anything. 

It's just... well, I feel terrible about this, but my temper has kind of been snapping for no reason. Like, the other day, dispatch made a tiny schedule change, and I just completely blew up at them. And then, um, I was playing pickup basketball, and this guy barely bumped me, and I just started cursing at him. Normally I'd just shake something like that off, no problem. I felt so bad about it after. I'm usually really professional and friendly, I promise. I just... I don't know why I'm acting like that. Is it normal to feel a little bit more irritable after something like this happens? I really hope I'm not coming across as aggressive or anything.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy since the incident in the holding room?

Um... lost interest? Well, I mean, I try to keep busy, you know? I think it's important to stay active and have hobbies. I don't want to sound like I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself or anything. 

But, um... I guess maybe I haven't been doing as much lately? Like, I usually love playing basketball on the weekends, but I just haven't really felt like going. And I haven't been watching the games on TV either, which is weird for me. I just... I don't know, I guess I've just been a little tired, so I haven't had the energy for it. I'm sure I'll get back into it soon, though. I really want to get back to my normal routine. That's okay, right? I mean, it's normal to take a little break from things sometimes, isn't it?
Have you been trying to avoid thinking about what happened in the holding room?

Um... avoid thinking about it? Well, I mean, I try to just focus on my work, you know? I want to be a reliable courier, so I try to just keep my mind on the job. I don't want you to think I'm running away from my problems or anything like that. 

But, um... I guess I have been making a few little changes to my routes lately. Nothing major, I promise! Just... well, I've been turning down the night runs. And, um, I've been kind of taking the long way around town so I don't have to drive anywhere near that detention building. It just... if I get too close, or if I try to talk about it, I start feeling like I'm right back in that room again, and I just... I really don't like that feeling. So I just try to keep my distance. That's a normal way to handle things, right? Just giving myself a little space so I can keep doing my job well? I really hope that doesn't make me sound weak or anything.
Have you been startled more easily since the incident in the holding room?

Um... startled easily? Well, I mean, as a courier, you kind of always have to stay on your toes, right? I've always prided myself on being really alert and steady behind the wheel. I definitely don't want you to think I'm a nervous wreck or an unsafe driver now or anything like that. 

But, um... I guess maybe my reflexes are just a little, I don't know, a little too dialed in right now? It's actually kind of embarrassing, honestly. Lately, if my dispatch radio crackles unexpectedly, or a police siren goes off, or even if someone just slams a car door nearby... I just jump. Like, I physically jump, like I'm about to get rushed all over again. 

And then my heart just starts pounding so incredibly hard. It gets so intense that I actually have to pull the van over for a minute, or step outside if I'm in the middle of dropping off a package, just to catch my breath and get it to stop. I always make sure I pull over safely, I promise! I'm still being really responsible about my job. But... that's a normal reaction, isn't it? Just my body being a little overly cautious after a scare? I really hope it goes away soon so I can just be back to my old self.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body, watching yourself, or like things aren't real?

Um... outside of my body? Like things aren't real? Well, I mean, I try to stay really grounded, you know? Being a courier, you have to be present and focused on the road. I definitely don't want you to think I'm losing my grip on reality or that I'm spacing out while I'm driving. I'm very careful about that.

But, um... no, I don't think I've felt anything like that. I haven't felt like I'm watching myself from the outside or anything strange like that. I mean, sometimes I get a little distracted thinking about my route, but I'm always right there in the driver's seat. That's a good thing, right? That means I'm still doing okay and staying connected to what I'm doing? I just really want to make sure I'm handling everything the right way.
Do you find yourself constantly looking over your shoulder or scanning your surroundings for potential threats?

Um... looking over my shoulder? Scanning for threats? Well, I mean, as a courier, you're always supposed to be aware of your surroundings, right? It's just part of being a safe driver and making sure the packages are secure. I definitely don't want you to think I'm, like, paranoid or acting suspicious while I'm out on my deliveries. I'm just doing my job.

But, um... no, I wouldn't say I'm constantly looking over my shoulder or anything like that. I mean, I check my mirrors like I'm supposed to, and I pay attention to who's around when I'm walking up to a building, but just the normal amount, you know? I don't feel like I'm always searching for danger or anything extreme. I'm just trying to be a responsible, observant worker. That's exactly what I should be doing, isn't it? Just keeping a normal eye on things so I can be good at my job? I really hope I'm doing it right.
Do you ever feel numb or disconnected from your body or the world around you?

Um... numb or disconnected? Like I'm not really there? Well, I mean, I always try to stay really engaged with people, you know? Like when I'm dropping off a package, I always make sure to smile and say hello to the receptionists or whoever's signing for it. I definitely don't want you to think I'm turning into some cold, unfeeling person who just ignores everybody. Being friendly is a big part of customer service.

But, um... no, I don't really think I feel numb or anything like that. I still care about doing a good job and being polite to people. I haven't felt disconnected from my body, either. I'm always moving around, carrying boxes, driving... I have to be pretty connected to my body to do all that heavy lifting! So, I'm just feeling things the normal way, you know? That's a positive sign, right? That I'm still staying present and doing my job properly? I just want to make sure I'm reacting to everything the way I'm supposed to.
Do you ever feel like you're in a daze or spaced out, even when you're in the middle of doing something?

Um... in a daze? Spaced out? Well, I mean, I really try to stay sharp, you know? Especially with driving all day and keeping track of the manifests. I definitely don't want you to think I'm just zoning out behind the wheel or ignoring my responsibilities. I take my job very seriously.

But, um... no, I don't think I get spaced out or anything. I mean, maybe I get a little tired at the end of a long shift, like anyone would, but I'm always paying attention to what I'm doing. I haven't been wandering around in a daze or anything like that. I'm keeping my focus where it needs to be. That's what you're supposed to do, right? Just keep pushing through and staying alert? I really hope that means I'm handling everything okay.
How long have you been avoiding the detention building and taking the long way around town?

Um... avoiding it? Well, I mean, I wouldn't really call it avoiding, exactly. I just... I found a different route that I prefer. I definitely don't want you to think I'm slacking off or wasting company time by taking a longer way. I still get all my deliveries done right on schedule, I promise. I just... I think it's better to take the scenic route sometimes, you know?

But, um... I guess I've been taking this new route for about a week now. Just... ever since that night I got detained and, um, saw that guy get assaulted in the holding area. I just thought, you know, maybe it's better to steer clear of that specific street for a little bit. Just to be safe, right? It's perfectly normal to want to take a different street after something like that, isn't it? I just want to make sure I'm making smart choices and being responsible. That's an okay reason to change my route, right?
Have you been avoiding people or places that remind you of the holding room?

Um... avoiding people or places? Well, I mean, I definitely wouldn't say I'm hiding from everyone or anything like that. I'm still working hard, still seeing my regular clients on the day shift. I really don't want you to think I'm just shutting down or not doing my job, because I'm definitely still working. 

But, um... I guess I have been turning down the night runs lately. And like I said, I've been taking the long way around town so I don't have to go near that detention building. It's just... I can't really make myself go over there right now. And I haven't really been talking to anyone about what happened, either. If I try to talk about it, or if I get too close to that building, I just start feeling like I'm right back in that holding room, and it's... it's a lot. So it just seems smarter to stay away from things that trigger that, right? That's a normal way to handle it, isn't it? Just focusing on the day shift and keeping my distance from the things that make it hard to work? I really hope that's an okay way to manage things for now.
Do you ever feel like you're observing yourself from outside your body or like you're in a dream?

Um... outside my body? Like a dream? No, no, definitely not. I mean, I want to assure you that I'm completely grounded in reality. I know who I am and where I am at all times, especially when I'm working. I wouldn't want you to think I'm losing my grip on things or that I can't be trusted to do my job properly. I'm very level-headed.

I don't think I've ever felt anything like that. No floating around or feeling like things aren't real. I'm just a regular guy trying to do his best and keep moving forward. That's a good thing, right? That I'm staying connected and not having those kinds of weird experiences? I just want to make sure I'm checking all the right boxes for being okay.
